711537.t: From Proto-Hellenic *súrks, *swə́rks, originally denoting "a piece of meat", from Proto-Indo-European *turḱ-s, a zero-grade s-stem nominal from the root *twerḱ- (“to cut”).

711563.t: Beekes claims a Pre-Greek origin, due to the semantic category of lizards being "local substrate" and not being conceptualized among the Proto-Indo-Europeans.

711555.t: Borrowed from Old Median *xšaθrapāvā, which is cognate with Old Persian 𐎧𐏁𐏂𐎱𐎠𐎺𐎠 (x-š-ç-p-a-v-a /⁠xšaçapāvā⁠/); see there for more.

711596.t: Usually derived from Proto-Indo-European *(s)gʷes- (“to extinguish, quell”).

711505.t: From a West Semitic language such as Hebrew סַפִּיר (sappîr); originally from Assyrian Akkadian šipirtu (“lapis lazuli”).

711577.t: Of obscure origin. Furnée tentatively considers the word to be from Pre-Greek, based on a presumed connection to σοφός (sophós, “clever”), though Beekes is skeptical.
